metadata.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
metadata.abstract_summary: Letting a language model explore and self-evaluate multiple candidate reasoning paths as a search tree - branching, backtracking, looking ahead - rather than committing to one left-to-right chain of thought, dramatically improves performance on tasks where early choices matter and dead ends are common: 4% to 74% success on the paper's own headline Game of 24 result, holding the base model constant

sections.heading: Claims
sections.text:
As the authors state it:

> Language models are increasingly being deployed for general problem solving across a wide range of tasks, but are still confined to token-level, left-to-right decision-making processes during inference. This means they can fall short in tasks that require exploration, strategic lookahead, or where initial decisions play a pivotal role. To surmount these challenges, we introduce a new framework for language model inference, Tree of Thoughts (ToT), which generalizes over the popular Chain of Thought approach to prompting language models, and enables exploration over coherent units of text (thoughts) that serve as intermediate steps toward problem solving. ToT allows LMs to perform deliberate decision making by considering multiple different reasoning paths and self-evaluating choices to decide the next course of action, as well as looking ahead or backtracking when necessary to make global choices. Our experiments show that ToT significantly enhances language models' problem-solving abilities on three novel tasks requiring non-trivial planning or search: Game of 24, Creative Writing, and Mini Crosswords. For instance, in Game of 24, while GPT-4 with chain-of-thought prompting only solved 4% of tasks, our method achieved a success rate of 74%.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: Evaluated on three tasks chosen specifically to require exploration or lookahead (the Game of 24 arithmetic puzzle, Creative Writing, Mini Crosswords), comparing Tree of Thoughts against standard prompting and chain-of-thought prompting on GPT-4, with the search strategy - BFS/DFS-style traversal, model-scored intermediate states - as the manipulated variable.

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- The Game of 24 result is large and clearly attributable to the search structure, since the input/output tokens and base model are held constant against the chain-of-thought baseline.
- Requires many more model calls per task than a single chain-of-thought pass, since each explored branch is its own call - a cost-vs-accuracy tradeoff the paper reports but does not fully resolve.
- The three tasks were selected precisely because they reward exploration; the paper does not claim, and later work has shown mixed results on, benefit for tasks where the first plausible reasoning path is usually already correct.
